q: The Monge problem (1781) seeks a transport map T: X → Y (with T_*μ = ν) minimising ∫c(x,T(x))dμ. The Kantorovich relaxation allows:
opts: Transport plans γ ∈ Π(μ,ν) (joint distributions with marginals μ,ν) — a convex relaxation of the Monge problem
exp: Kantorovich relaxation (1942): replace the Monge map T with a coupling (transport plan) γ ∈ Π(μ,ν), minimising ∫c(x,y)dγ(x,y). This is a linear program (convex) and always has a solution. Under the assumptions of Brenier's theorem, the optimal coupling is induced by a map T = ∇φ.
